status: Strategy A multiscale crustal-thickness/stretching/freeboard existence reconstruction; present coastline is a boundary condition, not an independently predicted observation

scope.continental_domain_method: All grid cells whose centers lie on either the Strategy A candidate or the generalized reference land mask are continental substrate. Additional nearest offshore cells are added in equal-area projected distance order until the Earth-analogue continental-crust area target is met. This treats candidate-only land as inherited/reworked crust that is emergent on Erde, reference-only land as continental crust submerged on Erde, and the remaining halo as submerged continental margin.
scope.coordinate_model: The grid is a present-material-coordinate freeboard mesh attached to the plate-block hierarchy. Rigid rotations are handled by plate-block-model.json; this model evolves thickness/elevation of those material cells and does not mistake Proposal 4's global reorientation for tectonic motion.
scope.late_quaternary_rule: Use authored Erde eustatic samples only at migration-critical late epochs. Deep-time snapshots use a zero long-term datum and classify cells within +/-150 m as shoreline-uncertain instead of inventing an exact global eustatic curve.

physical_constants.note: The Airy term is a first-order buoyancy term only. A bounded lithospheric/flexural residual is retained because observed elevation is not uniquely determined by Moho depth.

stable_interior.interpretation: Old craton/platform interior with a dense mantle lid; high freeboard does not require young uplift.

stable_margin.interpretation: Moderately stretched continental margin that remains emergent.

old_divergent_platform.interpretation: Candidate-only broad platform is not newly made land; it is an inherited Erde margin/platform whose breakup geometry diverged before the late Cenozoic.

reworked_margin_land.interpretation: Inherited margin thickened or reworked during older convergence; the surface becomes robustly emergent without net creation of continental crust.

orogenic_belt.interpretation: Shortening/thickening of inherited continental crust; present thickness remains within ordinary orogenic values.

submerged_reference_platform.interpretation: Reference-Earth land that is submerged continental platform on Erde after stronger or differently located Mesozoic extension and post-rift cooling.

extended_continental_margin.interpretation: Thin submerged continental/transitional margin. Final crust is thicker than normal oceanic crust and less stretched than the most hyperextended Zealandia examples.

jx1_junction.interpretation: Mostly old/reworked substrate thickened during 28-12 Ma assembly; later volcanic/erosional relief produces a continuous land neck by 3.2 Ma without late continental assembly.

c4_corridor.interpretation: Old foreland/microcontinental substrate thickened during 30-8 Ma collision; later glacial/isostatic effects are local perturbations, not the source of the corridor.

c3_se_shelf_head.interpretation: Shallow old continental shelf block remains close to sea level but landward shelf-cradle terrain stays available before H02.

arc_stepping_island.interpretation: Small old arc/microcontinental block with volcanic construction. It reaches durable emergence by 2 Ma, before all relevant eastern founding windows.

JX1_land_neck.pass_rule: all nodes remain above local relative sea level by 3.2 Ma and thereafter

NORTHERN_APPROACH_SHELF.pass_rule: H06 has at least two exposed founder-scale samples, H07 mixes exposure and inundation, and every H10 sample is exposed

EASTERN_SHELF_CHANNELS.pass_rule: shelf head and islands remain emergent while every channel remains submerged at the maximum tested lowstand

C4_PERIPHERAL_CORRIDOR.pass_rule: all warm-phase route nodes remain emergent; at least five of seven nodes remain emergent under the maximum cold-phase depression
